issues.description: Bookstore stored property name mismatch: The problem statement requires a class Bookstore that holds an array of Book instances named `books` and an initializer `init(books: [Book])` (problem_statement.md lines 8-12). In the solution implementation Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift the class declares the stored property as `let inventory: [Book]` (line 11) but the initializer is defined as `init(books: [Book])` and assigns to `self.books` (line 14). Additionally, the client code in Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift iterates `bookstore.books` (line 10). This inconsistent identifier usage (`inventory` vs `books`) contradicts the specification and causes a compilation error (undefined property `books`) and will confuse students about the correct property name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore implementation and its usages use a single consistent identifier. To match the problem statement and client usage, rename the stored property `inventory` to `books` (e.g. `let books: [Book]`) and update the initializer to assign `self.books = books`. Alternatively, if `inventory` is preferred, change the initializer signature to `init(inventory: [Book])`, assign `self.inventory = inventory`, and update all call sites (Client and problem statement) to use `inventory`. Prefer aligning the implementation to the problem statement (`books`) to avoid student confusion.
